project_title: The Zeigarnik Effect: Why Your Mind Obsesses Over the Unfinished

scenes.narration_text: Have you ever wondered why a cliffhanger in a movie, or a single unanswered text message, can hijack your entire night of sleep?
scenes.visual_prompt: Wide cinematic shot of a man sitting awake at 3 AM on the edge of his bed in a dimly lit apartment, staring at a glowing smartphone screen casting cold light across his face, rain streaking down the window behind him

scenes.narration_text: In nineteen twenty seven, a Russian psychologist named Bluma Zeigarnik sat in a crowded Vienna cafe, and noticed something strange about the waiters.
scenes.visual_prompt: 1920s Vienna grand cafe interior, warm amber chandeliers, a sharp-eyed waiter in a vest carrying a silver tray through bustling wooden tables, vintage European cinema aesthetic

scenes.narration_text: They could memorize complex orders from twelve different tables without writing a single word down. Yet the exact moment a bill was paid, their memory of that order vanished completely.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of a vintage brass cash register slamming shut on a marble counter, paper receipts floating in slow motion dissolving into golden dust particles in dark moody lighting

scenes.narration_text: Your brain treats every unfinished task like an open browser tab consuming background memory. Until the loop is closed, your subconscious refuses to let it go.
scenes.visual_prompt: Surreal cinematic macro shot of a human silhouette whose mind is illuminated by dozens of glowing suspended glass frames and clockwork gears spinning in a dark void

scenes.narration_text: To beat procrastination, never force yourself to finish a massive project. Just start for two minutes. Once the loop is open, your own brain will demand that you finish it.
scenes.visual_prompt: A contemplative man at a warm wooden desk at sunrise writing the very first sentence in a leather notebook with a fountain pen, golden morning light cutting through dark shadows
